text:
1.3 Example: Marketing Campaign
Marketing campaign data:

par(mar = c(.5, .1, 0, .1))
plot(x = X, y = rep(0, n), pch = 21, col = alpha("red", 0.5), bg = alpha("red", 0.5), cex = 3.5, axes = FALSE, ylab = "", xlab = "", xlim = c(-3,3))
axis(1, at = -2:2, line = -10, cex.axis = 3.5, lwd = 2, family="serif", mgp = c(3, 4, 0), tck=-0.05)








Research Question: Was the marketing campaign successful? Did it show a tendency (location-shift) toward significantly higher or lower sales?
Statistical Reformulation: Is the mean of \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) different from zero?
Testing problem: \(\hspace{1cm}H_0\colon \mu = 0\quad\) versus \(\quad H_1\colon \mu \neq 0\)
crumbs: 1  $p$-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.2 Cheat Sheet: Two-Sided \(t\)-Test

1.2.1 (See Lecture Hypothesis Tests)
Statistical hypothesis:

\(\displaystyle H_0\colon \mu = 0\quad\) versus \(\displaystyle \quad H_1\colon \mu \neq 0\)


\(t\)-test statistic: \[
\mathrm{T} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar{X} - 0)}{s}\overset{H_0}{\sim} t_{n-1}
\]
Setup:

Random (iid) sample: \(X_1,\dots,X_n\overset{\operatorname{iid}}{\sim}X\) with either

small sample size and \(X\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)\) or
large sample size (CLT, \(n\to\infty\)) and \(\mathrm{E}(X)=\mu\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(X)=\sigma^2\)



Empirical mean: \(\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\)

Empirical standard deviation: \(s = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar{X})}\)



Observed (obs) realization (marketing campaign):

\[
\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}} - 0)}{s_{\mathrm{obs}}} = 0.84
\]

Realized random sample: \(\{X_{1,obs},X_{2,obs},X_{3,obs},X_{4,obs},X_{5,obs}\}=\{0.64\), \(-0.72\), \(-0.23\), \(0.91\), \(1.06\}\)

Empirical mean: \(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_{i,obs} = 0.30\)

Empirical standard deviation: \(s_{\mathrm{obs}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_{i,obs}-\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}})} = 0.80\)

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.3 Critical Values \(\phantom{\mathrm{p}}\)







Critical Values: The critical values — the \((1-\alpha/2)\)- and the \(\alpha/2\)-quantiles of the \(t\)-distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=n-1\) — define the rejection regions for a given significance level \(0<\alpha<1\).



Marketing campaign data:

Density function of the \(t_{\operatorname{df}}\) distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=4\)


alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1
q_1    <- qt(p = alpha/2,   df=df)
q_2    <- qt(p = 1-alpha/2, df=df)

xx1    <- seq(-5, q_1, len=25)
yy1    <- dt(x = xx1, df = df)
##
xx2    <- seq(q_2,  5, len=25)
yy2    <- dt(x = xx2, df = df)

par(mar = c(4.5, .1, .1, .1))
curve(expr = dt(x = x, df = df),
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(-5, 5),
      ylim = c(0, .4), xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE)

polygon(x = c(xx1,rev(xx1)), y=c(yy1, rep(0,length(yy1))), border = NA, col = alpha("red", 0.25))
polygon(x = c(xx2,rev(xx2)), y=c(yy2, rep(0,length(yy2))), border = NA, col = alpha("red", 0.25))
axis(1, cex.axis = 2, family = "serif")
axis(1, at = T_obs, col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(1, at = q_1,   col = "red",  labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
lines(x = c(q_1,q_1), y = c(0, dt(x = q_1, df = df)), col="red")
axis(1, at = q_2,   col = "red",  labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
lines(x = c(q_2,q_2), y = c(0, dt(x = q_2, df = df)), col="red")
#mtext(side = 1, text = c(expression(q[alpha/2]), bquote(T[obs]==.(T_obs)), expression(q[1-alpha/2])), at = c(q_1,T_obs,q_2), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif")
mtext(side = 1, text = c(expression(q[alpha/2]), expression(T[obs]), expression(q[1-alpha/2])), at = c(q_1,T_obs,q_2), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif")
legend("topright", pch=c(22), cex=2.1, 
       col = alpha("red", 0.25), 
       legend=expression(alpha==0.05), 
       bty="n", pt.bg = alpha("red", 0.25))

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.3 Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value






\(\mathrm{p}\)-Value: The \(\mathrm{p}\)-value is the probability of observing a test statistic \(\mathrm{T}\) as extreme as \(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}\) or more extreme (in the direction(s) of the alternative hypothesis) than \(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}\), given the null hypothesis (\(H_0\)) is true.


Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value: \[\displaystyle\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \mathrm{P}\big(\,|\mathrm{T}|\,\geq |\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}|\;\big|\;H_0\;\text{is true}\big)\]





Marketing campaign data:

Density function of the \(t_{\operatorname{df}}\) distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=4\)


alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1
q_1    <- -abs(T_obs)
q_2    <- abs(T_obs)

pValue <- round(2 * min(pt(q_1, df = df), pt(q_2, df = df)), 2)

xx1    <- seq(-5, q_1, len=25)
yy1    <- dt(x = xx1, df = df)
##
xx2    <- seq(q_2,  5, len=25)
yy2    <- dt(x = xx2, df = df)

par(mar = c(4.5, .1, .1, .1))
curve(expr = dt(x = x, df = df),
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(-5, 5),
      ylim = c(0, .4), xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE)

polygon(x = c(xx1,rev(xx1)), y=c(yy1, rep(0,length(yy1))), border = NA, col = alpha("red", 0.25))
polygon(x = c(xx2,rev(xx2)), y=c(yy2, rep(0,length(yy2))), border = NA, col = alpha("red", 0.25))
axis(1, cex.axis = 2, family = "serif")
axis(1, at =  T_obs, col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(1, at = -T_obs, col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
mtext(side = 1, text = expression(-T[obs], T[obs]), at = c(-abs(T_obs),abs(T_obs)), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif")
legend("topright", pch=c(22), cex=2.1, 
       col = alpha("red", 0.25), 
       legend=bquote("p-value"==.(pValue)), 
       bty="n", pt.bg = alpha("red", 0.25))

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.4 Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value






\(\mathrm{p}\)-Value: The \(\mathrm{p}\)-value is the probability of observing a test statistic \(\mathrm{T}\) as extreme as \(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}\) or more extreme (in the direction(s) of the alternative hypothesis) than \(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}\), given the null hypothesis (\(H_0\)) is true.


Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value: \[\displaystyle\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \mathrm{P}\big(\highlight{|\mathrm{T}|} \geq |\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}|\;\big|\;H_0\;\text{is true}\big)\]





Marketing campaign data:

Density function of the Half-\(t_{\operatorname{df}}\) distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=4\)


library("extraDistr")

alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1
q_1    <- -abs(T_obs)
q_2    <- abs(T_obs)

pValue <- round(2 * min(pt(q_1, df = df), pt(q_2, df = df)), 2)

xx0    <- seq(0.00001, 5, len=50)
##
xx1    <- seq(-5, q_1, len=25)
yy1    <- dt(x = xx1, df = df)
##
xx2    <- seq(q_2,  5, len=25)
yy2    <- dt(x = xx2, df = df)
##
xx3    <- seq(abs(T_obs),  5, len=25)
yy3    <- dht(x = xx3, nu = df)

par(mar = c(4.5, .1, .1, .1))
plot(y = dht(x = xx0, nu = df), x = xx0,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(-5, 5),
      xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE, type="l")
lines(x=c(0,0), y = c(0,dht(x = xx0, nu = df)[1]), lwd=2)
curve(expr = dt(x = x, df = df), 
      lwd = 2, col = gray(.75), add = TRUE)


polygon(x = c(xx1,rev(xx1)), y=c(yy1, rep(0,length(yy1))), border = NA, col = gray(.95))
polygon(x = c(xx2,rev(xx2)), y=c(yy2, rep(0,length(yy2))), border = NA, col = gray(.95))
polygon(x = c(xx3,rev(xx3)), y=c(yy3, rep(0,length(yy3))), border = NA, col = alpha("red", 0.25))
axis(1, cex.axis = 2, family = "serif")
axis(1, at =  T_obs, col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(1, at = -T_obs, col = gray(.75), labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
mtext(side = 1, text = expression("|"~T[obs]~"|"), at = c(abs(T_obs)), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif")
legend("topright", pch=c(22), cex=2.1, 
       col = alpha("red", 0.25), 
       legend=bquote("p-value"==.(pValue)), 
       bty="n", pt.bg = alpha("red", 0.25))

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.5 Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value



Two-sided \(t\)-test:  \[\begin{align*}
\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{obs}}
& = \mathrm{P}\big(\,|\mathrm{T}|\,\geq |\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}|\;\big|\;H_0\;\text{is true}\big)\\[1ex]
& = 1 - \mathrm{P}\big(\highlight{|\mathrm{T}|}\leq |\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}|\;\big|\highlight{H_0\;\text{is true}}\big)\\[1ex]
& = 1 - \highlight{\mathrm{F}_{\,\text{Half-}t,n-1}}\big(|\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}|\big),
\end{align*}\] where \(\mathrm{F}_{\,\text{Half-}t,n-1}\) denotes the cdf of the Half-\(t\) distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=n-1\)


alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1

myfun <- function(x){1-pht(q = x, nu = df)}

par(mar = c(4.5, 9, 1, 0.5))
curve(expr = myfun,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(0, 4),
      ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE)
axis(1, cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(2, at = c(0,1), labels = c("0","1"), cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", las=2, mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(1, at =  T_obs, col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(2, at =  myfun(T_obs), col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.05)
lines(x = c(0,T_obs), y= rep(myfun(T_obs), 2), col="blue")
lines(x = rep(T_obs, 2), y= c(0, myfun(T_obs)), col="blue")
##
mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|"~T[obs]~"|"), at = c(abs(T_obs)), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif", hadj = 1)

Warning in mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|" ~ T[obs] ~ "|"), at =
c(abs(T_obs)), : "hadj" is not a graphical parameter

corners = par("usr") #Gets the four corners of plot area (x1, x2, y1, y2)
par(xpd = TRUE) #Draw outside plot area
text(x = corners[1]-.75, y = mean(myfun(T_obs)), bquote(p[obs]), srt = 0, cex = 2, family = "serif")


legend("top", lty = 1, lwd=2,
       legend=expression(1-F["Half-t,n-1"]), 
       bty="n", cex = 1.5)










library("extraDistr")
df <- 5-1

## 1 minus the distribution function of the Half-t
p_obs <- 1 - pht(q = abs(T_obs), nu = df)



There’s a one-to-one mapping between \(|\mathrm{T}_{obs}|\) and \(p_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

\(p_{\mathrm{obs}}\) effectively measures how extrem the value of \(|\mathrm{T}_{obs}|\) is, given that \(H_0\) is true.

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.6 Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value


Marketing campaign data:

\(|\mathrm{T}_\mathrm{obs}|=0.84\)
\(\alpha = 0.05\)

\((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of \(t_{4}\colon\) \(\mathrm{q}_{1-\alpha/2}=2.78\)




alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1

myfun <- function(x){1-pht(q = x, nu = df)}

par(mar = c(4.5, 9, 1, 0.5))
curve(expr = myfun,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(0, 4),
      ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE)
axis(1, cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(2, at = c(0,1), labels = c("0","1"), cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", las=2, mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(1, at =  T_obs, col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(2, at =  myfun(T_obs), col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.05)
axis(1, at =  qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.1)
axis(2, at = alpha, col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.05)
lines(x = c(0,T_obs), y= rep(myfun(T_obs), 2), col="blue")
lines(x = rep(T_obs, 2), y= c(0, myfun(T_obs)), col="blue")
lines(x = c(0,qt(1-alpha/2, df=df)), y= rep(alpha, 2), col="red")
#lines(x = c(0, 0), y= c(0, alpha), lwd = 3, col = "red")
lines(x = rep(qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), 2), y= c(0, alpha), lwd = 1, col = "red")
##
mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|"~T[obs]~"|"), at = c(abs(T_obs)), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif", hadj = 1)

Warning in mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|" ~ T[obs] ~ "|"), at =
c(abs(T_obs)), : "hadj" is not a graphical parameter

mtext(side = 1, text = bquote(q[1-alpha/2]), at = qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif", hadj = 1)

Warning in mtext(side = 1, text = bquote(q[1 - alpha/2]), at = qt(1 - alpha/2,
: "hadj" is not a graphical parameter

corners = par("usr") #Gets the four corners of plot area (x1, x2, y1, y2)
par(xpd = TRUE) #Draw outside plot area
text(x = corners[1]-.75, y = mean(myfun(T_obs)), bquote(p[obs]==.(round(myfun(T_obs), 2))), srt = 0, cex = 2, family = "serif")
text(x = corners[1]-.75, y = alpha, bquote(alpha==.(alpha)), srt = 0, cex = 2, family = "serif")

legend("top", lty = 1, lwd=2,
       legend=expression(1-F["Half-t,n-1"]), 
       bty="n", cex = 1.5)










We fail to reject \(H_0\colon\mu = 0\). That is, we have no statistical evidence that the marketing campaign showed a tendency toward significantly higher or lower sales.






⚠️ Failing to reject \(H_0\) does not mean that \(H_0\) is true. It only means that we do not have enough evidence to reject it.

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.7 Two-Sided \(\mathrm{p}\)-Value
Equivalent test decisions at the significance level \(0<\alpha<1\):




Critical values: Reject \(H_0\colon \mu =0\) if \(\displaystyle|\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}}| > q_{1-\alpha/2}\), where \(q_{1-\alpha/2}\) denotes the \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of the \(t_{\operatorname{df}}\) distribution.




\(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Reject \(H_0\colon \mu =0\) if \(\displaystyle\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{obs}} < \alpha\)




alpha  <- 0.05
df     <- 5-1

T_2obs <- 3.7

myfun <- function(x){1-pht(q = x, nu = df)}

par(mar = c(4.5, 9, 1, 0.5))
curve(expr = myfun,
      xlab = "", ylab = "", main = "",
      lwd = 2, col = 1, xlim = c(0, 4),
      ylim = c(0, .2), xaxs="i",yaxs="i", axes = FALSE)
axis(1, cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(2, at = c(0,1), labels = c("0","1"), cex.axis = 1.75, family = "serif", las=2, mgp = c(3, 1, 0))
axis(1, at =  T_2obs, col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.11)
axis(2, at =  myfun(T_2obs), col = "blue", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.05)
axis(1, at =  qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.1)
axis(2, at = alpha, col = "red", labels = FALSE, tck=-0.05)
lines(x = c(0,T_2obs), y= rep(myfun(T_2obs), 2), col="blue")
lines(x = rep(T_2obs, 2), y= c(0, myfun(T_2obs)), col="blue")
lines(x = c(0,qt(1-alpha/2, df=df)), y= rep(alpha, 2), col="red")
#lines(x = c(0, 0), y= c(0, alpha), lwd = 3, col = "red")
lines(x = rep(qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), 2), y= c(0, alpha), lwd = 1, col = "red")
##
mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|"~T[obs]~"|"), at = c(abs(T_2obs)), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif", hadj = 1)

Warning in mtext(side = 1, text = bquote("|" ~ T[obs] ~ "|"), at =
c(abs(T_2obs)), : "hadj" is not a graphical parameter

mtext(side = 1, text = bquote(q[1-alpha/2]), at = qt(1-alpha/2, df=df), line = 3.5, cex = 2, family = "serif", hadj = 1)

Warning in mtext(side = 1, text = bquote(q[1 - alpha/2]), at = qt(1 - alpha/2,
: "hadj" is not a graphical parameter

corners = par("usr") #Gets the four corners of plot area (x1, x2, y1, y2)
par(xpd = TRUE) #Draw outside plot area
text(x = corners[1]-.75, y = mean(myfun(T_2obs)), bquote(p[obs]), srt = 0, cex = 2, family = "serif")
text(x = corners[1]-.75, y = alpha, bquote(alpha==.(alpha)), srt = 0, cex = 2, family = "serif")

       legend=expression(1-F["Half-t,n-1"]), 
       bty="n", cex = 1.5)

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.8 \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing

While the \(\mathrm{p}\)-value can be a useful statistical measure, it is commonly misused and misinterpreted. (Wasserstein and Lazar (2016), Wasserstein, Schirm, and Lazar (2019))
“Scientific method: Statistical errors.” Nuzzo (2014)
ScienceNews (Siegfried 2010): “It’s science’s dirtiest secret: The ‘scien- tific method’ of testing hypotheses by statistical analysis stands on a flimsy foundation.”

Figure 1.1 shows the observed sales differences \[

Figure 1.1: Sales differences (sales after minus before the marketing campaign).










Assumption: There are no systematic differences (mean-shifts) between sales before and after the marketing campaign, other than the potential impact of the campaign itself.





Research Question: Was the marketing campaign successful? Did it show a tendency (location-shift) toward significantly higher or lower sales?
Statistical Reformulation: Is the mean of \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) different from zero?
Testing problem: \(\hspace{1cm}H_0\colon \mu = 0\quad\) versus \(\quad H_1\colon \mu \neq 0\)

title: 1  \(\mathrm{p}\)-Values: Challenges for Hypothesis Testing
text:
1.2 Repetition: Two-Sided \(t\)-Test






More Details: See our lecture on hypothesis testing for more details.



Statistical hypothesis:

\(\displaystyle H_0\colon \mu = 0\quad\) versus \(\displaystyle \quad H_1\colon \mu \neq 0\)


\(t\)-test statistic: \[
\mathrm{T} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar{X} - 0)}{s}\overset{H_0}{\sim} t_{n-1},
\] where \[
\bar{X}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i
\] denotes the empirical mean and \[
s = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar{X})}
\] denotes the empirical standard deviation.
Setup:

Random (iid) sample: \[
X_1,\dots,X_n\overset{\operatorname{iid}}{\sim}X
\]
Small sample size: \[
X\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)
\]
Large sample size (CLT, \(n\to\infty\)): \[
\mathrm{E}(X)=\mu\quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{Var}(X)=\sigma^2
\]


Observed (obs) realization (marketing campaign):

\[
\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}} - 0)}{s_{\mathrm{obs}}} = 0.84
\]

Realized random sample: \(\{X_{1,obs},X_{2,obs},X_{3,obs},X_{4,obs},X_{5,obs}\}=\{0.64\), \(-0.72\), \(-0.23\), \(0.91\), \(1.06\}\)

Empirical mean: \(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_{i,obs} = 0.30\)

Empirical standard deviation: \(s_{\mathrm{obs}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_{i,obs}-\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}})} = 0.80\)


Critical Values \(\phantom{\mathrm{p}}\)






Critical Values: The critical values — the \((1-\alpha/2)\)- and the \(\alpha/2\)-quantiles of the \(t\)-distribution with \(\operatorname{df}=n-1\) — define the rejection regions for a given significance level \(0<\alpha<1\).

\(t\)-test statistic: \[

\bar{X}&=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\\
s      &= \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(X_i-\bar{X})}
\end{align*}\]
denote the empirical mean and the empirical standard deviation.






Assumptions:

For large sample sizes (CLT, \(n\to\infty\)): \[

\]





Observed (obs) realization (marketing campaign):

\[
\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{obs}} = \frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}} - 0)}{s_{\mathrm{obs}}} = 0.84
\]

Empirical mean: \(\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^5 X_{i,obs} = 0.30\)

Empirical standard deviation: \(s_{\mathrm{obs}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{5-1}\sum_{i=1}^5(X_{i,obs}-\bar{X}_{\mathrm{obs}})} = 0.80\)


Critical Values \(\phantom{\mathrm{p}}\)
